overview: This table holds the words the game shows for items, money, player titles and nicknames, and shop unlock messages in each language.
description: Localized item names, money/count display templates, nickname and title labels, and shop unlock messages. Item and PlayerCardTitle/PlayerCardNickname rows reference this table through Id_ItemText; GameItem helpers add type-specific parameters before resolution. ItemSet rows have the same schema column, but all exported sets leave it as None and derive set names from member items.

ID.simple: The name that links this text to an item, player title, nickname, or shop message so the game knows which words to show.
ID.technical: FName ID in FGameDataTableRow_GameText (export ImportKeyField Id), matched to the row name; all 11 exported language shards have the same 4,817 keys with ID equal to the row key. FindTextRow scans the 14-table GameText array in order and returns the first table holding the id, so there is no ITM_ prefix dispatch and an earlier-table collision or an empty Text still stops the search. SYS_-prefixed ids are routed to SystemText instead. Item.Id_ItemText feeds GameItem_GetNameText/GameItem_GetNameTextCore (or GameItem_GetNameTextById); ItemSet.Id_ItemText is a schema field but all 2,402 exported ItemSet rows set it to None, so GameShop_GetItemSetNameText uses money/nickname templates, then Set->Id_ItemText, then the first item's id. PlayerCardTitle/Nickname Id_ItemText feeds title/nickname label requests; nickname ids may be suffix-swapped by PlayerCard_MakeNicknameTextId. Shop unlock text and nickname set templates use hard-coded ITM_UNLOCK_MESSAGE_* / ITM_NICKNAME_* ids. The table is loaded as ItemTextDataTable_<LoadedLanguageName> in slot 3 (index 2) of the combined GameText array.

Text.simple: The words the player sees, such as an item name or shop unlock message. Some lines leave room for a character name, amount, or nickname.
Text.technical: FString row text (+0x10), copied by GetGameText and run through FormatText. tags are filled from the glossary map rebuilt from GlossaryTextDataTable_, and tags from the request parameters; other tag types are left as-is. The En export has 492 GLO and 97 DYN occurrences and two runs, with no bracket modifiers in any shard. ITM_MONEY_1001 is ''; the three cosmetic wrapper rows combine and ; ITM_NICKNAME_1001/1002 combine and ; 74 ITM_UNLOCK_MESSAGE_* rows use caller-supplied keys such as VALUE. GameItem_GetNameTextCore supplies ITEM_VALUE as an int32 only when bWithValue=true (digits grouped through SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0124/0123/0122 by GroupDigits, with optional width flags); when bWithValue=false Money bypasses this table and returns a raw grouped-number request. For Costume/CustomVoice/SituationOverviewPose it redirects to the three wrapper ids, with ITEM_NAME as the item's own Id_ItemText resolved as a nested request and CHARACTER_NAME from Character.Id_GlossaryText_Name. Item effect descriptions are not ItemText rows: GameItem_GetDescriptionText takes EquipmentItemEffect.Id_BattleText (BattleTextDataTable) and supplies VALUE from EffectValue[0], or BuffDebuff.FloatValue[0] when the buff row is found and its type is not 0x1D; Extras use BTL_ITEM_BUFF_MESSAGE_1000. runs are rendered by the rich-text inline decorator only when the id resolves to a brush in CustomImageSet. A missing row or an empty string yields empty text; empty rows vary by shard (0 in En/Ja/Ko, 165 De, 1,974 each Zh_Hans/Zh_Hant), and HasGameTextContent tests for emptiness before title/nickname labels are used.

notes: FGameDataTableRow_GameText has 11 exported language shards with 4,817 identical ids each (ID equals the row key in every row). The runtime builds ItemTextDataTable_<LoadedLanguageName> from EApplicationLanguage and appends it as the third table (index 2) of 14; Config/DefaultGame.ini:35-45 cooks one TextDataTable_<Lang> variant per chunk. The enum also names Ar/Ind/Pl/Ru/Th, for which no companion export is available.

Cross-table joins: Item.Id_ItemText -> this table for names (2,724 of 2,769 non-None references in the En export resolve; the other 45 are STR_STDM_SS_* short-story ids outside this table). ItemSet.Id_ItemText is None in all 2,402 exported sets, whose five Id_Item/Quantity entries are aligned; GameShop_GetItemSetNameText instead uses ITM_MONEY_1001 with ITEM_VALUE=Quantity[0], nickname pairs ITM_NICKNAME_1001/1002 with NICKNAME_TOP/BOTTOM from Id_Item[0]/[1], then Set->Id_ItemText, then First->Id_ItemText (GameShopSaleItemListItemDataBase.cpp:1201-1245). PlayerCardTitle/Nickname Id_ItemText -> labels with an empty-text twin fallback by Id_Item (GamePlayerCardParameter.cpp:517-566). Equipment descriptions are a separate join: EquipmentItemEffect.Id_BattleText -> BattleTextDataTable with DYN=VALUE from EffectValue[0] or BuffDebuff.FloatValue[0] (buff type 0x1D keeps the effect value); Extras use BTL_ITEM_BUFF_MESSAGE_1000 (GameItemDescriptionTextWidget.cpp:235-271).

Some ids are used only after transformation: PlayerCardNickname has 1,482 _TOP and 1,482 _BOTTOM rows; PlayerCard_MakeNicknameTextId swaps the suffix for languages 2/3/5/9/10 (Fr/Es/It/Es_LA/Th), while nickname set templates already print BOTTOM before TOP in several shards. ITEM_NAME and CHARACTER_NAME are nested requests, so the literal row name seen in a widget may differ from the displayed string.

Lookup and caching: GetText routes only SYS_ ids to SystemText; all other ids scan TextDataTables in array order (FindTextRow, 0x14af290). TextDataTables are rebuilt only in AGameTextManager::Tick after all language loaders complete, skipping null tables; glossary parameters are rebuilt from the glossary shard before OnCultureTextLoaded. There is no per-row cache (some UI code freezes a resolved string into a raw-text request via GameShop_MakeResolvedText), and a missing or empty row simply renders empty. Free-battle and visual-lobby costume selectors also map costumes to Id_ItemText (GameFreeBattleTeamCharacterSelectWidget.cpp:316, GameVisualLobbyCharacterSelectVariationWidget.cpp:266).

Reconstruction caveat: status/functions.json marks GetGameText (0x14af510), GetTextById (0x14afde0), GameItem_GetNameTextById (0x12ca160) and SetItemRow (0x1545580) as byte-matched, while GameItem_GetNameTextCore (0x12ca260, DV30), the description/extra helpers (0x12c9d00 NA06, 0x12c8be0 NA08), GameShop_GetItemSetNameText (0x12cac30), FindTextRow (0x14af290 NA15) and Tick (0x14c96f0 BG03) are behaviour-certified; GameItem_GetNameText (0x12ca700) has equal bytes but a HOLD verdict. Content is partial; no retail runtime or Blueprint-only uses are claimed.

usages.detail: GameItem_GetNameText passes the nullable Item row's Id_ItemText and ItemType to GameItem_GetNameTextCore; null rows produce an empty request.

GameItem_GetNameTextCore redirects Money/Costume/CustomVoice/SituationOverviewPose/Nickname ids and adds ITEM_VALUE, ITEM_NAME, CHARACTER_NAME or the nickname suffix swap; Money with bWithValue=false uses GroupDigits only.
GameItem_GetNameTextById resolves an item id through ItemDataTables and then Id_ItemText through the same helper.
Title requests start from a plain Id_ItemText request and HasGameTextContent; nickname requests at :548 use the suffix-swapped transformed id with the same empty-text twin fallback.
Item-set names use Money's ITEM_VALUE from Quantity[0], nickname templates with the first two items' text ids, then Set->Id_ItemText and First->Id_ItemText in that precedence.
A matching shop lineup appends GetGameText of the hard-coded ITM_UNLOCK_MESSAGE_4050 after the lineup unlock text.
Calls GetGameText(GameItem_GetNameText(Row, 0, true)) and keeps unlocked title rows only when the rendered string has more than one character.
FindTextRow scans the ordered GameText table array and returns the first matching row; ItemText is third, and only SYS_ ids bypass it for SystemText.
Text blocks resolve requests through GetText; the rich-text inline decorator handles runs when the id maps to a brush.
Rank rewards request cosmetic item names with value 1 and bWithValue=false, so Money-style quantity formatting bypasses the table.
